content:
incident-bot: ALERT: high-rate GPU OOMs in us-west1 (hotpool-2). Multiple model-server containers restarting during prefill of long-context requests. Customer-facing 5xx spike ~2.3%. Paging @alice-oncall @dave-sre. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/prefill-oom

alice-oncall: on it, grabbing logs and topology. Status checks in progress.

ben-runtime: seen repeated oom_killer + cuda OOM from prefill path. Sample kernel output:
```
[13342.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (model-server) total-vm:...kB, anon-rss:...kB
CUDA Error: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
```
Prefill sequences hitting ~30k tokens, KV cache allocation spike all-at-once.

alice-oncall: can we short-circuit large-prefill requests ASAP? Any fast toggles?

ben-runtime: yes. We can enable runtime-side prefix_trim and prefill_shedder. Patching runtime to set prefill_prefix_trim=2048 and enable prefill_shed=true. Rolling now.

carla-ml: immediate ML-router rule: divert prefill_token_count > 12000 to gptx-7b-q4 (quantized) or return 413 with guidance. I'll push the rule and a short banner for developers.

dave-sre: isolating noisy node i-0c0ffee7 where most restarts originate. Draining now:
```
kubectl drain i-0c0ffee7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl scale deployment/gpu-hotpool-2 --replicas=$((CURRENT+2)) -n inference
```
Scaling up +2 nodes to reduce allocation packing.

ellen-cs: I have two paying customers flagged who hit 5xx at 12:10 UTC. Sending them an interim update.

frank-support: logs show first spike ~12:08 UTC, majority of errors between 12:08-12:18. Capturing for customer note.

alice-oncall: mitigation checklist (short): 1) prefix_trim=2048 (applied) 2) route >12k tokens to q-variant (carla) 3) add temporary gateway max_prefill_tokens=15000 4) scale hotpool + drain noisy nodes 5) create alert for SIGKILLs

ben-runtime: runtime patch deployed; crash frequency down by ~60% but one container still flapping due to KV cache growth. Captured stacktrace from failing container:
```
#0 cuMemAlloc
#1 runtime/kv_cache.c:kv_alloc_all(+) 0x1f4
#2 runtime/prefill.c:do_prefill
#3 server/request.c:handle_request
```
Looks like attempt to allocate KV cache for seq_len ~32768 all at once -> failure.

carla-ml: pushed routing rule + soft-429 path for very large prefill to avoid full allocation. Also enabling quantized fallback for large-context requests.

dave-sre: new nodes added (i-0deadbeef, i-0f00babe). Drained i-0c0ffee7; node showed repeated SIGKILLs from oom_killer per dmesg.

ben-runtime: short-term follow-ups I'm doing: 1) add prefill_kv_alloc_bytes metric 2) change prefill allocator to incremental-reserve (chunked cuMemAlloc) 3) temporary auto-evict KV when prefill_kv_alloc > 60% GPU mem. Rolling metrics now.

ellen-cs: customer bulletin sent: "We identified a GPU memory issue affecting a subset of very long-context requests. Engineering has applied mitigations (trimming and routing). We expect normal service in ~20-40 minutes; follow-up postmortem to come." :email:

frank-support: error rate dropped to ~0.9% after trims + routing. Timeouts mostly gone.

alice-oncall: handing to @dave-sre for watch and follow-ups. Please escalate if error_rate >1.5% or any new restarts.

dave-sre: taking over. Created ticket INF-8433. Follow-ups:
- enforce hard gateway limit request_max_prefill_tokens=16384
- add alert for prefill_kv_alloc_bytes > 70% of gpu_mem
- postmortem to include replay test for long prefill sequences

ben-runtime: set temp alert and dashboard. Also added short-term log entry prefill_chunk_alloc to track incremental allocations.

carla-ml: long-term plan: adaptive_kv_shrink + incremental prefill allocation + model-side early-bail for extremely long contexts. Will open RFC.

dave-sre: marking incident mitigated at 6832123725 (error-rate back to baseline, no restarts in last 12m). Leaving INF-8433 open for postmortem + fixes.

ellen-cs: notified affected customers with mitigation summary and PM link.

alice-oncall: thanks all. Closing pager. Action items: gateway hard limit, allocator incrementalization, perf test for seq_len 32k. Will close this thread in 2h if no regressions.
